sections.label: Rising traveller volume at checkpoints
sections.summary: Traveller volume has continued to rise across all checkpoints and is expected to return to pre-pandemic levels by 2024 and increase thereafter.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: First, traveller volume has continued to rise across all our checkpoints.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: It is expected to return to pre-pandemic levels by 2024 and continue to increase thereafter.

sections.label: Biometric departure at Changi Airport
sections.summary: The departure journey at Changi Airport will be biometric-enabled end-to-end from the first half of 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Next, to enhance the traveller experience at Changi Airport, the departure journey will be biometric-enabled, end-to-end, from the first half of 2024.

sections.label: Disclosure of passenger and crew information
sections.summary: The Minister is proposed to be empowered to authorise disclosure of passenger and crew information to the airport operator for four specific use cases.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To facilitate this initiative, it is proposed that the Minister be empowered to authorise the disclosure of passenger and crew information to the airport operator for specific use cases, namely: (a) bag drop, access control and gate boarding; (b) passenger tracing within the airport for security purposes; (c) offloading of baggage for passengers who did not board the flight; and (d) verification of travellers' identity and tax liability for duty free purchases and Goods and Services Tax (GST) refunds.

sections.label: Amendments on passenger and crew lists
sections.summary: Clauses 21 to 27 amend sections and introduce new sections to impose accuracy requirements on passenger and crew lists and let ICA collect information from bus operators and other land transport modes.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clauses 21 to 27 amend sections 22 to 23B and introduce new sections 23C, 23D, 23E and 23F to, among other things, impose requirements on the accuracy of the lists of passengers and crew furnished by transport operators, in addition to completeness and timeliness.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: These amendments will enable ICA to also collect passenger and crew information from bus operators as well as the particulars of persons travelling through our land checkpoints via other modes of land transport such as cars, trucks or motorcycles or on foot.

sections.label: No-Boarding Directives against undesirable persons
sections.summary: Clause 9 introduces section 9AA to empower the Controller of Immigration to issue No-Boarding Directives against undesirable persons to prevent them boarding an in-bound conveyance.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clause 9 introduces the new section 9AA to empower the Controller of Immigration – henceforth, "the Controller" – to issue to one or more persons for an in-bound conveyance, which I will refer to as the transport operator for brevity, No-Boarding Directives (NBDs) against undesirable persons, whether they wish to enter or transit through Singapore, to prevent them from boarding the in-bound conveyance at the point of departure.

sections.label: Amendments to false information offences
sections.summary: Clause 57 replaces an offence with a new false or misleading information offence, introduces a strict liability offence, and provides that these offences apply even if information was provided outside Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clause 57 amends section 57 to: (a) replace the section 57(1)(k) offence with a new offence of knowingly giving information that is false or misleading, or omitting any thing, without which the information is misleading.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This offence will be punishable with a fine of up to $8,000 or imprisonment of up to 12 months or both; (b)	introduce a new strict liability offence under Section 57(1)(ka) for obtaining or attempting to obtain an immigration facility by giving such false or misleading information, which will be punishable with a fine of up to $4,000; (c)	provide that these offences apply even if the applicants had provided the false or misleading information while outside of Singapore.

sections.label: Immigration officers direct persons to remain
sections.summary: Clauses 28 to 31 amend sections 24 to 26 to empower immigration officers to direct persons to remain at an immigration depot or designated place until they leave Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clauses 28 to 31 will amend sections 24 to 26 to empower immigration officers to direct such persons to remain at an immigration depot or at a place designated by the Controller, until arrangements are made for them to leave Singapore.

sections.label: Controller empowered to repatriate persons
sections.summary: Clauses 36, 37, 40 and 57(i) empower the Controller to repatriate other categories of persons ordered removed, including illegal immigrants and persons who remained unlawfully.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clauses 36, 37, 40 and 57(i) will introduce amendments to similarly empower the Controller to repatriate other categories of persons who have been ordered to be removed from Singapore, including "illegal immigrants" and “persons who remained unlawfully in Singapore”.

sections.label: Arrest and vehicle detention in non-immigration cases
sections.summary: Clause 55 introduces new sections 51AB to 51AE to let immigration officers arrest persons in non-immigration cases and detain their vehicles pending handover to law enforcement.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clause 55 therefore introduces new sections 51AB to 51AE to allow immigration officers to arrest persons involved in such non-immigration cases and detain any vehicle driven by them or which is under their control, pending the handover of custody to the relevant law enforcement agency.

sections.label: Fine in lieu of caning
sections.summary: Clause 58 introduces a new section 58A to allow courts to impose a fine in lieu of caning on such an offender.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To address this, clause 58 of the Bill introduces a new section 58A to allow the courts to impose a fine in lieu of caning on such an offender.

sections.label: Removal of statutory appeals to Minister
sections.summary: Clauses 7, 12, 13, 16, 33 and 37 remove a foreigner's right to make statutory appeals to the Minister for Controller decisions affecting his stay in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To this end, clauses 7, 12, 13, 16, 33 and 37 remove the right of a foreigner to make statutory appeals to the Minister for decisions made by the Controller affecting his stay in Singapore.

sections.label: Clarifying loss of PR status
sections.summary: The Bill introduces amendments to clarify at law when PR status is lost, defining permanent resident of Singapore and circumstances leading to loss of PR status.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: However, this means that the PR had effectively lost his PR status during the period between the REP expiry and PR reinstatement.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This Bill will introduce amendments to the Act to clarify at law when the PR status is lost, by introducing a definition of “permanent resident of Singapore” and setting out the circumstances that will lead to the loss of PR status.

sections.label: MHA sets six-month period
sections.summary: The Ministry for Home Affairs intends to set this period at six months.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Ministry for Home Affairs (MHA) intends to set this period at six months.

sections.label: No reinstatement after PR loss
sections.summary: Six months is enough for PRs to regularise status, so there is no avenue for reinstatement once a PR loses PR status under the revised framework.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Given that six months is more than enough time for PRs to regularise their status, there will be no avenue for reinstatement once a PR loses his PR status in accordance with the revised framework.

sections.label: Repeal of Banishment Act
sections.summary: Clause 61 repeals the Banishment Act 1959, which allows the Minister to remove a foreigner from Singapore and is no longer relevant today.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In particular, clause 61 repeals the Banishment Act 1959.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Banishment Act, which also allows the Minister to remove a foreigner from Singapore, is no longer relevant today, and hence we propose to repeal it.

sections.label: Woodlands and Tuas checkpoint crossings
sections.summary: Woodlands Checkpoint sees more than 350,000 daily crossings, and over 1.7 million people crossed Woodlands and Tuas checkpoints from 31 August to 4 September 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Woodlands Checkpoint ranks amongst the world’s busiest border crossing with more than 350,000 passing through every day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Just over the long weekend of the Presidential Election from 31 August 2023 to 4 September 2023, more than 1.7 million people crossed Woodlands and Tuas checkpoints.

sections.label: Fines for immigration offenders
sections.summary: The revised sentencing approach proposes fines in lieu of an extended prison term for immigration offenders exempted from or medically unfit for caning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, the revised approached to sentencing when dealing with immigration offenders, I note that it is proposed that fines be introduced in lieu of an extended prison term for immigration offenders convicted of immigration offences and who are exempted from or found to be medically unfit for caning.

sections.label: Fine default imprisonment term
sections.summary: Replacing caning with a fine under section 319 can lead to a default imprisonment term of up to two and a half years, more than the 12-month period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As was mentioned by the hon Minister, if he is not medically fit to take caning, then the Court can replace the caning sentence with an imprisonment term of not more than 12 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: But with the replacement of the caning with a fine sentence, by applying section 319, because the punishment is more than two years, the upper limit of the scale would apply; in which case the default imprisonment term can go up to two and a half years – which is more than the 12-month period for not receiving a caning sentence.

sections.label: Repeal of immigration provisions
sections.summary: Proposes repealing section 8(4A) and notes proposed section 39B removes any opportunity to be heard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In addition, it is proposed that current section 8(4A), which requires the Controller to inform a person the class of prohibited immigrants of which, in the opinion of the Controller, the person is a member of, be also repealed too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For the benefit of hon Members, there are 15 classes in the Immigration Act, ranging from a person who is believed to have no means of supporting himself or herself, or believed to be a prostitute or believed to be a person who advocates the overthrow of the government by violence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Also, under the proposed section 39B of the Act, it is provided that the Controller is not required to give any person, who may be affected by his decision, an opportunity to be heard.

sections.label: Retaining statutory appeal to Minister
sections.summary: Questions why the law is changed when Malaysia and Brunei retain the statutory appeal to their Minister.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Hence, the question arises, if it ain’t broken, why fix it?

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I would also like to point out that, as a matter of comparative law, countries such as Malaysia and Brunei which have similar history and similar pieces of legislation as our Immigration Act, still retain the statutory appeal to the equivalent of our Minister.

sections.label: Advance Passenger Information collection
sections.summary: Asks whether public transport operators like the RTS Link operator or SBS Transit must collect API or be exempt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, on the proposal to allow immigration officers to collect Advance Passenger Information (API), I would like to enquire if it is proposed that public transport operators such as the operator of the Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link that is due to be commissioned in about three years’ time or SBS Transit that operates service no 170 will have the obligation to collect API or would they be exempt?

sections.label: Sentencing policy for immigration offenders
sections.summary: States the proposed sentencing amendments do not weaken the tough stance against immigration offenders, traffickers and harbourers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I have carefully reviewed the proposed amendments in the Bill dealing with sentencing policy in the Immigration Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I do not believe they represent a derogation from our uncompromising stance against immigration offenders as well as traffickers and harbourers of illegal and prohibited immigrants, that the law will deal with them firmly by imprisonment, caning or fine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It is important to maintain this tough stance so that we do not backslide to the situation several decades ago when we had a serious illegal immigrant problem that affected Singaporeans' safety and security.

sections.label: Manual counters under NCC
sections.summary: Asks whether manual counters will no longer be an option for Singaporean travellers once the NCC is fully rolled out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, Minister of State Faishal told the House on 21 April that under the NCC, all manual counters and automated lanes will be replaced in phases with the next generation automated border clearance system gates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Does this mean that once the NCC is fully rolled out, the use of manual counters will no longer be an option for Singaporean travellers?

sections.label: Contingency plans for NCC upgrade
sections.summary: Asks what additional contingency plans ICA will put in place so the NCC upgrade does not cause immigration disruptions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As shared by Minister of State Faishal in April, some of these capabilities will be implemented in a form and manner not used or tested elsewhere.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I also recall that the four-and-a-half-hour disruption to immigration systems on 31 March was caused by a failed upgrade to the multimodal biometric system (MMBS).

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What additional contingency plans will ICA put in place to ensure that the upgrade to the NCC will not cause immigration disruptions of that scale or worse?

sections.label: Pre-Marriage LTVP Assessment uptake
sections.summary: ICA introduced the PMLA in 2015, but fewer than half of about 7,200 annual LTVP applicants completed it before applying.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2015, ICA introduced the Pre-Marriage Long-Term Visit Pass Assessment or PMLA to give prospective cross-national couples an indication that the foreign spouse is likely to qualify for an LTVP after the marriage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, since the PMLA was introduced, out of an annual average of 7,200 LTVP applications, only 3,000 applicants or less than half had completed the PMLA prior to applying for the LTVP, according to a reply by the Minister to my question last month.

sections.label: LTVP eligibility letter outcomes
sections.summary: Of 3,000 foreigners issued LTVP eligibility letters, only 1,900 were eventually granted LTVP or LTVP-Plus status.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In another reply to me last month, the Minister revealed that only 1,900, out of the 3,000 foreigners issued with letters of LTVP eligibility, were eventually granted LTVP or LTVP-Plus status, which means 37% were not.

sections.label: Immigration criteria transparency
sections.summary: ICA should provide more criteria transparency in the immigration framework, similar to the COMPASS framework for employment passes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Third, ICA should provide more criteria transparency in the immigration framework similar to the Complementarity Assessment (COMPASS) framework for employment passes.

sections.label: Bill removes PR appeal right
sections.summary: The Bill removes the statutory right of appeal to the Minister on ICA decisions on granting, revoking and varying conditions of PRs' permits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Bill removes the statutory right of appeal to the Minister on the decisions made by ICA on granting, revoking and varying conditions attached to PRs' permits.

sections.label: Reconsideration and appeal information
sections.summary: MHA stated PR applicants and PRs may seek ICA's reconsideration, but the ICA website lacked information on submitting appeals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And I note from MHA's statement that PR applicants and PRs may seek ICA's reconsideration of its decisions, particularly if there are new facts that were not previously submitted to ICA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, when searching the ICA website, I could not find much information on submitting appeals for failed LTVP or PR applications.

sections.label: Online immigration appeals channel
sections.summary: An accessible self-service channel and secure online form should be available on the ICA website for all immigration appeals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: An accessible, self-service channel should be made available, particularly for appeals with a substantial volume.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A secure online form should be made available on the ICA website for all immigration appeals, with clear instructions guiding appellants to submit new facts that were not previously submitted or provided in their earlier application.

sections.label: NBDs for bus transport operators
sections.summary: NBDs for land transport operators raise operational questions about feasibility for buses given dynamic schedules and connectivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Third, the introduction of NBDs for transport operators of land-based conveyances, has raised some operational questions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: There have been concerns about the practical feasibility of implementing NBDs for buses, especially considering the dynamic nature of bus schedules and connectivity with different bus services and transport modes.

sections.label: Digital permits at land checkpoints
sections.summary: Accepting digital versions of permits and passes raises a question about initial congestion at land checkpoints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Fourth, the shift towards accepting digital versions of permits and passes to verify immigration status and declaration of goods raises a question about initial potential congestion, particularly at our land checkpoints.

sections.label: Money laundering and entry denial
sections.summary: A $1.8 billion money laundering investigation shows the need for a more rigorous system to deny entry to malicious individuals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The recent high-profile $1.8 billion money laundering investigation underscores this point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Some individuals may exploit the guise of business and investments to engage in unlawful activities once they enter and reside in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We need to do our best to deny entry to individuals who have malicious intentions to commit crimes within our borders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To achieve this, the implementation of a more rigorous system is essential, safeguarding the safety and security of our nation and residents.

sections.label: Queueing time at checkpoints
sections.summary: The passage asks authorities to explain improvement measures to reduce queueing time at Woodlands and Tuas checkpoints and calculate efficiency changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the authorities explain in detail what improvement measures we will implement to reduce the queueing time at Woodland and Tuas checkpoints?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can we calculate whether efficiency will increase or decrease in percentage terms?

sections.label: ICA advance passenger information powers
sections.summary: Proposed sections 23C and 23D empower ICA to collect advance passenger and crew information for bus entry into Singapore's checkpoints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Under the proposed sections 23C and 23D, the ICA will be empowered to collect advance passenger and crew information for entry into Singapore’s checkpoints via buses.

sections.label: NBDs to deny boarding
sections.summary: Introducing NBDs to direct transport operators to deny boarding to undesirable individuals is a crucial enhancement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In addition, the introduction of NBDs to direct transport operators to deny boarding to undesirable individuals, particularly those who pose a threat to our safety and security, is a crucial enhancement.

sections.label: Digital permits verify immigration status
sections.summary: Amendments propose digital permits and passes to verify immigration status, using a token and biometrics at automated touchpoints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Under the amendments, it is now proposed that digital versions of permits and passes can be used to verify immigration status.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Under this initiative, the passenger's digital identity and flight information undergo backend processing to generate a unique token, which is then used along with their biometric data to confirm their identity and travel details at different automated touchpoints.

sections.label: NCC cross-border regional integration
sections.summary: The NCC would make Singapore a trendsetter, and a Member asks if regional partners will integrate it as a cross-border initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Next, the NCC will put Singapore as trendsetter in the global security landscape.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: However, additional value will be created for Singapore and our visitors if other jurisdictions come on board and integrate the NCC in their security administration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry share whether there are plans for us to work with regional partners to integrate the NCC as a cross-border initiative?

sections.label: Circumstances improving Home Team effectiveness
sections.summary: A Member asks under what circumstances the changes improve Home Team operational effectiveness, which the passage says address technological, traveller and threat challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Could the Minister share more on under what circumstances would the proposed changes improve Home Team’s operational effectiveness?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: These changes are essential to adapt to the evolving challenges posed by technological advancements, increasing traveller demands, and emerging threats.

sections.label: Changi Airport passenger movement figures
sections.summary: Changi Airport passenger movement totalled 32.2 million last year and is expected to return to 68.3 million by 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Last year, passenger movement at Changi Airport totalled 32.2 million and is expected to return to pre-COVID-19 traffic of 68.3 million by 2024.

sections.label: Automated clearance enrolment and NCC
sections.summary: Over four million foreign visitors from 51 jurisdictions enrolled in automated clearance since May 2022, and the next NCC allows passport-free departure from 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Since May 2022, more than four million foreign visitors from 51 jurisdictions have enrolled in the automated clearance initiative and cleared immigration with their biometric details.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The next NCC will allow residents and visitors leaving Singapore to clear immigration without having to use their passports from 2024.

sections.label: System disruption affecting automated lanes
sections.summary: A system disruption affected all automated departure lanes at four airport terminals and Woodlands and Tuas Checkpoints, and some passengers missed flights.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: All automated departure lanes in all four airport terminals as well as at Woodlands and Tuas Checkpoints were affected by this system disruption and some passengers missed their flights.

sections.label: Bus operators' passenger information difficulties
sections.summary: Bus operators say they face difficulties submitting passenger information before vehicles reach Woodlands and Tuas checkpoints and worry about fraudulent identities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Bus operators had expressed that they are facing difficulties in submitting passenger information before their vehicles arrive at the Woodlands and Tuas checkpoints.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: They are also worried that some passengers might use fraudulent identities.

sections.label: Online SG Arrival Cards for foreigners
sections.summary: The speaker suggests foreigners entering via land checkpoints submit SG Arrival Cards online three days before arrival, with ICA informing affected passengers and assisting senior small operators.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: To get around this problem, I would like to suggest that foreigners entering Singapore via the land checkpoints, submit SG Arrival Cards online three days before their arrival.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This way, ICA can inform any affected passengers directly on any entry concerns.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I hope ICA will assist these rather senior small operators who are not tech-savvy with their operating costs.

sections.label: Automated clearance for passengers, vehicles, cargo
sections.summary: The amendments allow further automated clearance for passengers, vehicles and cargo.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The amendments allow further automated clearance for passengers, vehicles and cargo.

sections.label: Causeway daily crossings
sections.summary: Currently, around half a million people cross the Causeway every day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Currently, around half a million people cross the Causeway every day.

sections.label: PRs losing status yearly
sections.summary: The passage asks how many PRs lose their status each year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The first is, how many PRs lose their status each year?

sections.label: Assurance for PRs' status
sections.summary: The speaker says PRs could be assured their status is likely permanent as long as they reside in Singapore and are law-abiding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For many, it is part of a journey to citizenship, while for others, they could be husbands, wives or parents of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I think it would be helpful if PRs can be given assurance that their status is likely to be permanent as the name suggests as long as they reside in Singapore and are law-abidding.

sections.label: PR status appeal rights
sections.summary: The Bill removes the right of appeal on the grant and revocation of PR status, though applicants and PRs can seek ICA's reconsideration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill will remove the right of appeal on the grant and revocation of PR status.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: MHA has clarified that PR applicants and PRs can still seek ICA’s reconsideration.

sections.label: Other appeal rights removed
sections.summary: The Bill also removes rights of appeal against decisions such as removal of persons unlawfully remaining in Singapore and entry and re-entry permits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Additionally, the Bill removes rights of appeal against other decisions such as the removal of persons unlawfully remaining in Singapore and entry and re-entry permits.

sections.label: Controller publishing condition changes
sections.summary: New subsection 4A of section 10 lets the Controller publish condition changes on a prescribed website or in the Gazette instead of notifying individuals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new subsection 4A of section 10 states that the Controller may publish any changes to conditions on a prescribed website or in the Gazette instead of giving notice to individuals if the Controller assesses that it is not practicable to give notice to every individual.

sections.label: Border control IT reliability
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Ministry will ensure the reliability and security of IT systems at border controls.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: How will the Ministry ensure the reliability and security of our IT systems at border controls?

sections.label: Cybersecurity, backups, biometrics privacy
sections.summary: The passage asks about backup plans and modes of operation, and how the Ministry will protect data privacy since biometrics are not replaceable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Even as the Ministry seeks to up our cybersecurity, let us continue to have backup plans and modes of operation as part of our resilient ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would also like to ask how the Ministry will protect the data privacy of individuals since biometrics are not replaceable.

sections.label: Plans for elderly people
sections.summary: The passage asks what the Ministry's plans are to deal with this problem as more people will be senior or elderly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What are the Ministry’s plans to deal with this problem as more of our people will be senior or elderly?

sections.label: Falsified identification document cases
sections.summary: Asks how many persons were caught using falsified identification documents in the last three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In the last three years, how many persons had been caught using falsified identification documents?

sections.label: ICA clearance procedures at Changi
sections.summary: The Bill supports ICA's new procedures, including streamlined Changi Airport clearance using a digital token at automated touchpoints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces provisions to support ICA’s new procedures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This includes streamlining the clearance experience at Changi Airport, where a person’s biometric and flight information will be processed backend using a unique digital token at the various automated touchpoints.

sections.label: Advance passenger information and NBDs
sections.summary: Clause 27 expands ICA's advance passenger information collection to all entry modes and allows NBDs to transport operators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I now turn to future-proofing against evolving challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I note that clause 27 of the Bill expands ICA’s powers to collect advance passenger information from currently, vessels, airlines and train operators, to across all modes of entry including from bus operators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: ICA will also be able to issue NBDs to direct transport operators to deny the boarding of undesirable individuals, particularly those who pose a threat to our safety and security.

sections.label: Recovering repatriation funds from offenders
sections.summary: Clause 51 empowers ICA to recover repatriation funds from all persons to be removed, not just prohibited immigrants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I next move on to the enhancing of border controls and the administration of passes and permits, and on this point, with respect to the recovery of funds from offenders for their repatriation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I welcome clause 51 of the Bill, which empowers ICA to recover funds from all categories of persons to be removed from Singapore and not just prohibited immigrants.

sections.label: Records held as potential threats
sections.summary: It currently holds around 99 million records, all of which are potential threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Today, it currently holds around 99 million records, all of which are potential threats.

sections.label: Multiple identity immigration offences spike
sections.summary: Travellers entering Singapore with a false or different identity rose from 28 in 2021 to 441 in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: In Singapore, the number of travellers attempting to enter Singapore using a false identity or one different from their past trips jumped from 28 in 2021 to 441 in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: This is a 15-fold spike in multiple identity cases and a rise in immigration offences in 2022.

sections.label: Immigration amendment safeguards borders
sections.summary: The amendment, comprising these initiatives and enhanced immigration officer powers, will further safeguard security and keep borders safe.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: As such, this amendment, comprising of these initiatives and the enhancement of the powers of immigration officers will further safeguard our security and keep our borders safe.

sections.label: ICA officers trained for NCC
sections.summary: ICA has trained officers since 2020, and around 4,000 can take on higher-value assessment and investigation jobs using new skills.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To prepare for this NCC, ICA has been training its officers since 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Mr Choo will be glad to know that as a result, around 4,000 ICA officers are able to take on higher-value jobs in assessment and investigation, using newly acquired skills such as investigative interviewing and profiling.

sections.label: Liquidated damages from vendors
sections.summary: ICA and HTX can and will pursue liquidated damages from a vendor if systems fail to meet required standards.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: ICA and HTX can and will pursue liquidated damages from a vendor if the systems fail to meet the required standards.

sections.label: No foreign data sharing yet
sections.summary: Sharing such data with other governments or foreign airport operators to facilitate immigration clearance for Singaporeans abroad is not yet on the cards.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: As for the questions Mr Gerald Giam and Mr Vikram Nair raised, whether such data will be shared with other governments or foreign airport operators so as to facilitate immigration clearance for Singaporeans abroad, for security reasons this is not yet on the cards.

sections.label: False passport prosecution cases
sections.summary: Between 2020 and 2022, 38 cases involving the use of false passports or travel documents were prosecuted in court.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Between 2020 and 2022, there were 38 cases prosecuted in court involving the use of false passports or travel documents.

sections.label: Digital Long-Term Passes issued
sections.summary: Since February 2023, ICA only issues digital Long-Term Passes.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Since February 2023, ICA only issues digital Long-Term Passes.

sections.label: Public bus operators excluded
sections.summary: The Bill excludes public bus operators from submitting advance passenger information and from complying with the NBDs.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Bill specifically excludes public bus operators from the submission of advance passenger information or to comply with the NBDs.

sections.label: Undesirable travellers denied entry
sections.summary: Before the COVID-19 pandemic, a monthly average of 110 undesirable travellers were denied entry into Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Prior to the COVID-19 pandemic, there was a monthly average of 110 undesirable travellers denied entry into Singapore.

sections.label: Repatriation expenses cases and funds
sections.summary: From 2018 to 2022, there were 74 cases and more than $53,000 of Government-aided funds used for repatriation expenses.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: From 2018 to 2022, there were 74 cases and more than $53,000 of Government-aided funds used for repatriation expenses.

sections.label: Amendment for five or more offenders
sections.summary: He asked why the amendment applies to offenders convicted of employing five or more immigration offenders, since they are likely Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: First, he asked why our amendment applies to offenders convicted of employing five or more immigration offenders, since they are likely to be Singaporeans.

sections.label: Caning extension to unfit males
sections.summary: The amendment extends the provision to males sentenced to caning for this offence but later found medically unfit for caning.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Our amendment does nothing more than extend this provision to males who are sentenced to caning for this offence but are subsequently found medically unfit for caning.

sections.label: Imprisonment term for fine default
sections.summary: Mr Murali Pillai asked why the Bill does not limit imprisonment for an offender who cannot be caned but defaults on the fine.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Second, Mr Murali Pillai asked why there is no provision in the Bill to limit the length of the imprisonment term that the Court can impose on an offender who cannot be caned but defaults on the fine imposed in lieu.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We agree with him, that in such cases, it would be ironic if the imprisonment for defaulting on a fine is longer than the prison term that could have been imposed in lieu of caning.

sections.label: PR status loss and appeals
sections.summary: About 7,900 PRs yearly lose status by being outside Singapore without a valid Re-Entry Permit, and most who appealed succeeded.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To Mr Vikram Nair's question, on average, 7,900 or less than 2% of the total PR population each year lose their PR status by being outside of Singapore without a valid Re-Entry Permit.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Of those who appealed, the majority were successful as they had valid reasons for not renewing their Re-Entry Permit in time.

sections.label: Biometric clearance and Woodlands Checkpoint
sections.summary: From 2024, Singaporeans and departing visitors will use biometrics instead of passports, and ICA will redevelop Woodlands Checkpoint.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Three, progressively from 2024, Singaporeans and departing visitors will no longer need to present their passports for immigration clearance and will instead verify their identity through biometrics, reducing clearance time in bus halls by up to 40%.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Four, over the longer term, ICA will redevelop Woodlands Checkpoint to enhance clearance for all types of vehicular traffic and reduce travel times, especially during peak periods.

sections.label: Biometric data sharing conditions
sections.summary: Sharing biometric data with other governments or foreign airport operators is premature, requiring secure technology and mutual acceptance of safeguards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: Without this, the applicants will tend to just keep trying to apply with the same information and not really realising why is it they cannot make the cut.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It is really premature for us to consider what steps might make it possible for us to proceed with sharing of biometric data with other governments or foreign airport operator.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The technology must be secure enough and there must be also mutual acceptance of the additional safeguards that must be put in place.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Without knowing exactly what those conditions need to be, I do not want to speculate on what approvals may be needed.

sections.label: Support for families and applicants
sections.summary: The approach has been facilitative, particularly for families with children and applicants with long-established family ties, and will continue.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The broad context is that we have been facilitative, particularly for families who have children, for applicants whose family ties are long-established and we will continue to support them in this process.
